statement: Let $r$, $s$ and $t$ be the three roots of $x^3 - 4x^2 - 5x + 7 = 0$. What is $(r + s)(s + t)(t + r)$?

choices.misconception: I took the product of the roots to be 7 instead of -7, so I computed 4 times -5 minus 7.
I multiplied the sum of the roots by the sum of the pairwise products, 4 times -5, and forgot to subtract the product rst.
I used the evaluation trick but put a minus sign in front, thinking (4 - r)(4 - s)(4 - t) equals -P(4).
I took the sum of the roots to be -4 instead of 4, so I computed -4 times -5 minus -7.

hints: Each factor is a sum of two roots. What is the sum of all three?
Since $r + s + t = 4$, the factors are $4 - t$, $4 - r$ and $4 - s$. Compare with $P(x) = (x - r)(x - s)(x - t)$.

solutions.reliable: By Vieta's formulas, $r + s + t = 4$, $rs + st + tr = -5$ and $rst = -7$. Expanding, $(r + s)(s + t)(t + r) = (r + s + t)(rs + st + tr) - rst$. So the value is $4 \cdot (-5) - (-7) = -20 + 7 = -13$. The transferable idea: symmetric expressions in the roots can be rebuilt from the coefficients.
solutions.elegant: Because $r + s + t = 4$, we have $r + s = 4 - t$ and so on. Since $P(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 - 5x + 7 = (x - r)(x - s)(x - t)$, the product is $(4 - r)(4 - s)(4 - t) = P(4) = 64 - 64 - 20 + 7 = -13$.
